newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says to brief US on budget, reforms, economy.
newsitem.headline: MOF says to brief US on budget, reforms, economy.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference he intended to tell U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers during a meeting on Tuesday about Japan's budget, reforms, and its basic stance on the economy.

Mitsuzuka said he would tell Summers about the parliamentary discussions on the budget currently going on in Japan, its administrative, fiscal, and financial system reforms, and MOF's basic stance on the economy.
"I hope to deepen understanding and strengthen cooperation," he said.
Mitsuzuka said the meeting of the six markets in Tokyo on Tuesday would be an important one for Asian economies as well as for the reform of Japan's financial system.
He added that the meeting was a meaningful one and he hoped it would be held on a regular basis.
Mitsuzuka said he was aware of comments made by Summers and U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and would listen to them as the opinions of the United States.
However, Japan had repeatedly explained its monetary and fiscal policy and its intention to carry out reforms during various meetings like those of the Group of Seven nations.
On Friday, Summers warned Japan against trying to export its way out of its economic problems and urged it to restore domestic demand-led growth and repair its financial system.
Mitsuzuka also said that he did not think that continuing special income tax cuts in Japan would contribute much to activating the economy.

He said he hoped parliament would pass the state budget for the next fiscal year starting in April without revisions, but the government would do its best to reduce spending as it was now carrying out fiscal reforms.
Asked whether special income tax cuts might be one option in any talks with other parties after the budget is passed, Mitsuzuka said the ministry was not considering these.
Mitsuzuka also said he would like a decision made on interest rates on MOF deposits by Friday and at the latest by Tuesday.
Welfare Minister Junichiro Koizumi has been opposing the Finance Ministry's efforts to lower interest rates paid on Welfare Ministry deposits at MOF.
